html:
The Somali Civil War began with the fall of Siad Barre in January 1991, when rebel armies took Mogadishu and the Somali state collapsed.

Clan militias fought over Mogadishu and the farm lands of the south, and famine in 1992 killed hundreds of thousands. A United Nations and United States mission brought food but left after the Battle of Mogadishu. For years Somalia had no national government at all.

An Islamic Courts Union briefly united Mogadishu in 2006, before Ethiopia invaded and al-Shabaab rose. A federal government recognised abroad has slowly rebuilt, with African Union troops. Meanwhile the north broke away as Somaliland, and millions joined the diaspora.
sum: The Somali Civil War began with the fall of Siad Barre in January 1991, when rebel armies took Mogadishu and the Somali state collapsed.
